If I rank w first, I have priority 1. If I get it, great! If not, I'd go to my second choice.

Let's consider the case where I rank z first and get rejected. Then I go to x. If I rank x second, I have priority 2.

If I rank y first, I have priority 1. But I really don't like y.

Since most applicants favor y > x > w > z, z and x are less competitive. I should try for z first, then x. If I get rejected from both, I'd rather have w than y.

Therefore, I'll rank z > x > w > y.
